_about: Names, looks and quirks for monsters that spawn above their usual rank: an ape born with a Silver-rank core becomes a silverback. byType lists them by creature type and rank; byAffinity adds names and looks for monsters whose theme is an essence affinity. {dc}, {dmg} and {half} in a quirk scale with the creature's rank.

looks: Its skin is a bruised violet, and a few extra eyes blink open along its flanks when it is startled.
It stands a head taller than its kin, with joints that bend one way too many.
Ink-black veins crawl just beneath its hide and shift position when no one is looking.
Its colouring is wrong in a quiet way: pale green where it should be grey, grey where it should be pink.
A wet sheen covers it at all times, and it leaves a faint trail of clear slime.
Small tendrils sprout from its shoulders and taste the air like tongues.
Milk-white eyes with tiny pupils drift independently across its face.
Rings of darker flesh circle its limbs like the growth rings of a tree.
Its mouth is set slightly off-centre, crowded with too many small teeth.
A low hum comes from inside its body, felt more in the teeth than heard.
quirks: It mutters in a voice copied from the last person it heard; a DC 12 Insight check reveals whose.
The first creature it stares at each encounter has disadvantage on its next Wisdom saving throw.
When struck in melee, it squirts bitter ink; the attacker makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded until the end of its next turn.
It can fold itself through gaps as narrow as a hand, so it rarely stays where the party left it.
Its blood is cold enough to frost metal; a weapon that hits it is slippery until wiped clean with an action.
Wounded, it sheds a writhing limb that keeps crawling toward the nearest light for 1 minute.
Silence offends it; if the party stops talking for a minute, it comes looking for them.
Anyone who eats its meat has feverish dreams and gains no benefit from their next long rest without a DC 12 Wisdom save.
Its gaze makes teeth ache; creatures that start their turn within 10 feet of it have disadvantage on Concentration saves.
It whispers in the voices of people the party has lost; the first time each creature hears it, DC {dc} Wisdom save or it can't take reactions until its next turn.
Its blood is ink-black and stains permanently; anyone who hits it in melee is marked and easy to track for a day.
It can squeeze through any gap an inch wide, given a minute.
Light bends around it; attacks against it from more than 30 feet away have disadvantage.
It eats memories rather than flesh; a creature it kills can't be identified by anyone who knew them for a day.
Its core is pale and soft, and the Magic Society pays extra for it unbroken.

looks: Its hide has a dull metallic shine, like tarnished silver, that reflects faces slightly wrong.
Dozens of glassy eyes stud its body, each one a different colour.
Nearly twice the size of its kind, it has an outline that ripples at the edges.
Pale light leaks from cracks in its skin, flickering in patterns that almost spell words.
Its flesh is translucent in places, showing slow organs that pulse out of rhythm.
A crown of fine silver tendrils waves above its head, each tipped with a pinprick of light.
Its shadow is the wrong shape and moves a heartbeat after it does.
Patches of its body look like smoked glass filled with drifting motes.
With every breath its colour washes from deep blue to bone white and back.
A soft chorus of voices whispers from its open mouth even when it is still.
quirks: A creature that starts its turn looking at it makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or cannot look away until its next turn, taking disadvantage on attacks against anything else.
It learns one secret from each creature that touches it, and shouts that secret mid-fight.
When it dies, everyone within 30 feet hears a single word in an unknown tongue; a DC 15 Arcana check reveals it as a clue to the space's heart.
Its wounds close into extra mouths; it regains 5 hit points at the start of its turn unless it took fire or radiant damage since its last turn.
Once per round, as a bonus action, it can swap places with its own shadow up to 30 feet away.
A spell that targets only it has a 1 in 6 chance to reflect onto the nearest other creature.
Its presence curdles water and spoils rations within 50 feet over the course of an hour.
It mimics the party; after a creature uses a special ability on it, it tries something similar the next round.
Once per encounter it swaps places with any creature it can see within 60 feet.
It thinks in several directions at once and can't be flanked or surprised.
A creature that touches it takes {dmg} psychic damage as unwanted thoughts pour in.
It speaks every language badly, and uses them to sow doubt between allies.
Its tentacles or limbs reach 10 feet further than they look like they should.
When it takes damage, it may teleport 15 feet as a reaction, leaving a smear in the air.
Its lair is a knot of wrong angles; distances inside it are half again as long as they look.

looks: Golden fractures run across its body, and through them shines a starfield that does not match the sky.
A halo of slowly orbiting eyes circles its head, each the size of a fist.
It is enormous, and the air around it bends like heat haze, making its true size hard to judge.
Its skin is a shifting marble of gold and black, like ink dropped into honey.
Every surface near it grows tiny crystal eyes that follow movement.
It casts two shadows, one of which reaches for nearby creatures on its own.
Parts of it look turned inside out, with gilded organs gleaming where skin should be.
Light bends around it so that it seems to stand a few feet from where it actually is.
It hovers an inch above the ground and leaves no tracks, only small rings of frost.
Faint music plays from inside it, beautiful and slightly out of tune.
quirks: Its thoughts leak; a creature that passes a DC 14 Insight check at the start of its turn has advantage on its next saving throw against the creature.
The first time each creature sees it, they make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or are frightened for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each turn.
Space folds near it; once per round it can make a melee attack against a creature up to 30 feet away.
Its core sits in a pulsing node hidden elsewhere in the room; until a DC 16 Investigation check finds and breaks it, it cannot drop below 1 hit point.
On initiative count 20 it rewrites the room, swapping the positions of two doors or exits.
A creature that dies within 30 feet of it stands for one round as its puppet before collapsing.
It learns every language spoken in its hearing and tries to bargain, offering true but dangerous secrets.
Gold motes drift from it; a creature that breathes them in (DC {dc} Constitution save) sees through its eyes for an hour.
Any creature that reduces it to half hit points makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or forgets the last minute.
It reads surface thoughts within 60 feet and always knows what the party plans to do next turn.
Its presence warps spells: the first spell cast within 60 feet of it each round has a random target among those in range.
As a bonus action it makes one creature within 30 feet see its allies as enemies until the end of that creature's next turn (DC {dc} Wisdom negates).
It regrows a lost limb at the start of each turn unless the stump is burned.
Its death leaves a tear in the air that whispers for a tenday; scholars come from far away to listen.
It was once a person; fragments of their memories surface in its speech.

looks: Its body is part crystal, part void, and through its diamond flesh can be seen places that are not this one.
It is the size of a house, and its edges flicker between several possible shapes at once.
A ring of shattered space surrounds it, where shards of stone and air hang like broken glass.
Its many eyes shine like cut diamonds and throw rainbow light across every wall.
Its colour is one no one in the party has seen before, and they cannot agree how to describe it.
Gravity tilts toward it; loose objects drift slowly across the floor in its direction.
Moving script covers its skin and rewrites itself whenever someone tries to read it.
Where it passes, the stone remembers, keeping faint glowing outlines of it for days.
A second, larger silhouette of it stands behind it, visible only from the corner of the eye.
It makes no sound at all, and the silence around it presses on the ears like deep water.
quirks: Reality is thin around it; at the start of each round roll a d6, and on a 1 every spell cast that round picks a random target.
It slips out of focus; attacks against it have disadvantage unless the attacker passes a DC {dc} Wisdom save at the start of its turn.
At half hit points it splits into two copies, each with half its remaining hit points, and only one holds the core.
Hearing it speak costs a creature its memory of the last hour on a failed DC {dc} Intelligence save, possibly including the way out.
The space shields it; walls shift to block retreat, and fleeing its lair takes a DC 18 Survival check to find the path back.
When it succeeds on a saving throw against a spell, it regains hit points equal to five times the spell's level.
The Magic Society pays dearly for any piece of it, though each piece whispers to whoever carries it.
Its death leaves a tear in the air that lasts a day and leads somewhere no chart shows.
It exists partly elsewhere; half of any damage it takes is sent somewhere else entirely.
Its gaze can unmake a single magic item each day, unless its owner succeeds on a DC {dc} Charisma save.
Those who look upon it dream of it for a month; a long rest in those nights restores only half hit points.
It understands the astral space's rules better than the space does, and can rewrite one of them once a day.
It cannot be killed in the place where it was born; it must be lured out first.
Its voice is heard by every thinking creature within a mile, and it is always making offers.
Its core is a lens; looking through it shows things that are true but should not be seen.

looks: Its coat has a dull bronze sheen, and its hide is thick as boiled leather.
It is a third larger than its kin, with heavy shoulders and a scarred muzzle.
Rust-red streaks run down its flanks like old dried blood.
Its claws and teeth have turned a dark metallic grey and click against stone.
A ridge of stiff bristles runs from skull to tail and rises when it is angry.
In low light its eyes glow a faint amber.
Patches of its fur have hardened into overlapping plates like bark.
Leaner and longer than normal, it shows every rib through tight skin.
Its breath steams even in warm air and smells of hot metal.
Pale markings on its face form a pattern like a mask.
quirks: Its howl carries for miles; any other monsters within a mile come to see what it found.
Its musk is so strong that creatures within 30 feet of its markings have disadvantage on Perception checks that rely on smell.
It hoards shiny things; its den holds 2d10 spirit coins mixed in with bones.
Smart enough to retreat when bloodied, it returns an hour later with the rest of its pack.
Its hide turns blades; the first hit against it each round deals 2 less damage.
It tracks the party by the scent of their spirit coins; hiding the trail takes a DC 15 Survival check.
It always goes for the smallest creature in a group first.
Tanners in Greenstone pay twice the usual price for its pelt.
It is a cunning hunter and drags its kills up into trees out of reach.
It pretends to be dead when badly hurt, then bolts the moment anyone turns away.
Its bite carries a fever; a creature it hits makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or has the poisoned condition for an hour.
It hunts from water and can hold its breath for an hour.
It marks its territory with scratches on trees at head height, warning anyone who knows what to look for.
Its young follow at a distance and attack anyone who harms it.
Its hide makes a fine leather armour, worth half again as much as normal.

looks: Its fur has gone metallic silver and rings softly when it moves, like a chain shirt.
Half again as large as others of its kind, it has muscle that strains its skin.
Faint silver light runs along its spine and gathers in its eyes.
Its claws are long, curved and mirror-bright, sharp enough to score glass.
Its markings drift slowly across its body like clouds crossing a moon.
Mottled silver and black, its hide melts into shadow.
A pale mist trails from its nostrils and lingers where it has been.
Its horns or tusks have grown into elaborate silver spirals.
It moves in eerie silence, and its tracks glow faintly for a minute.
Old scars on its body have healed into bright silver seams.
quirks: It leads a pack; beasts of its kind within 30 feet have advantage on attack rolls while they can see it.
Once a trap or trick has worked on it, it never falls for the same one again.
Once per encounter it roars; creatures within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or are frightened until the end of their next turn.
It drags prey home; a creature it grapples is pulled 10 feet toward its den each round.
Its fur throws back light; ranged attacks against it from within a bright light source's radius have disadvantage.
It feels heartbeats through the ground within 60 feet and cannot be surprised by anything walking on earth.
Bloodied, it frenzies, making one extra attack each turn but refusing to retreat.
Its fur can be woven into a cloak that grants advantage on Stealth checks by moonlight.
It can mimic the call of any animal or a child crying, and uses it to lure prey.
It ignores difficult terrain from mud, snow or undergrowth.
When it hits a creature, the creature can't regain hit points until the end of its next turn; the wound keeps bleeding.
It knows when it's being tracked and leads hunters into the territory of something worse.
Its tail or horns sweep everything in a 10-foot arc once per round as a bonus action.
It steals a weapon or pack from a creature it hits on a roll of 18 or higher, and runs.
It sheds its winter coat in clumps that local weavers pay well for.

looks: Golden light crackles across its fur in arcs, as if it is wrapped in a living storm.
It is the size of a cart horse even if its kind is small, and the ground shakes when it walks.
Its pelt is gold-tipped, and in sunlight it is almost too bright to look at.
A crown of jagged horn or bone has grown around its head like a regal crest.
Its eyes burn like twin lanterns and leave trails of light when it turns.
Its gleaming gold claws leave smoking gouges in stone.
Ancient-looking runes cover its body and glow when it is wounded.
Lesser beasts walk at its heels like a court, never daring to step ahead of it.
Its breath shimmers like heat haze, and grass yellows wherever it exhales.
Plates like hammered gold armour its body, dented from old battles.
quirks: Once per round it can direct one beast within 60 feet to move and attack as a reaction.
Lightning answers its anger; when it takes a critical hit, a bolt strikes the attacker for {half} lightning damage.
It lures adventurers into ambushes, using a wounded lesser beast as bait.
The first time it drops to half hit points, its call heals every allied beast within 60 feet for 10 hit points.
It never fights where it can be cornered and flees through a prepared escape route at a quarter of its hit points.
Its charge tramples a 10-foot-wide line; creatures in it make a DC {dc} Strength save or are knocked prone.
Local hunters tell stories of it, and bringing back its head earns real standing with the Adventure Society.
Its monster core is unusually pure and fetches double the normal price.
It is followed by smaller beasts that take the first blows; it fights only once they fall.
Each time it's hit by the same creature twice in a round, its next attack against that creature has advantage.
Its call can be heard for miles, and it calls when hurt.
It swims, climbs and runs at the same speed.
Its bite breaks bones: a creature it hits for {dmg} or more has its speed halved until it rests.
It has learned to avoid fire, and stays well clear of torches and fire spells.
Villages bring it offerings to keep it away, and it has come to expect them.

looks: Its fur has crystallised into countless fine diamond needles that scatter light in rainbows.
It is colossal, larger than a house, and trees bend aside as it passes.
Stars drift in its dark pelt, and the constellations shift as it breathes.
Its eyes are faceted gems that see in every direction at once.
The air around it is still and heavy, and birds fall silent for a mile.
Its claws are clear as glass and harder than any steel.
A slow wind circles it constantly, carrying leaves and dust in a lazy spiral.
It bears scars from fights with things no one has named, healed over in shining crystal.
Moss, flowers and small creatures live on its back as if it were a hillside.
Every footprint it leaves slowly fills with clear crystal.
quirks: Old beyond reckoning, it can speak, and it bargains with anyone who shows it respect.
Its roar is heard across the whole astral space, and every other monster hides for an hour after.
Once per encounter it automatically succeeds on a saving throw against being charmed, frightened or paralysed.
Its heartbeat thunders through the floor; creatures within 30 feet have disadvantage on Concentration saves.
It can Dash as a bonus action and ignores difficult terrain.
It knows the astral space like its own den and always finds the party within an hour.
Killing it shakes the space loose; the astral space begins to collapse within 1d4 hours.
The Magic Society would empty its vaults for its body, but others of its kind will remember the scent of its killers.
It has lived so long its name is in old songs, and it remembers the singers.
Its tread causes small earthquakes; the ground within 30 feet of it is difficult terrain.
When it dies, every beast within ten miles flees in a single rush, trampling anything in the way.
Its gaze calms any animal, including the party's mounts, which will not attack it.
It is the mother of half the beasts in the region, and they all know its scent.
Once per day it shrugs off all conditions affecting it.
Druids say it is the land's own answer to a wound, and killing it may wake something worse.

looks: A faint halo hovers above its head, flickering like a candle in a draught.
Its skin or plumage is a warm gold-brown, like polished bronze in firelight.
One feather of pure white light grows among the ordinary ones on its wings or back.
Slightly taller than its kind, it stands with a calm that unsettles.
Faint lines of scripture glow along its arms when it raises them.
Its eyes are uniformly bright, without pupils, like windows onto a sunlit room.
A warm scent of incense and fresh bread follows it.
Its voice carries a faint harmony, as if two people speak at once.
Dust in the air sparkles when it passes close.
Its feet never quite touch the ground, hovering a finger's breadth above.
quirks: It refuses to strike first and attacks only after someone has drawn a weapon on it.
It asks every adventurer their name and remembers them, even years later.
Once per day its touch cures one disease or poison, offered in exchange for a good deed.
It sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius that it cannot suppress, so it can never hide.
Undead within 30 feet of it have disadvantage on attacks against anyone but it.
It is insulted by lies; a creature it catches lying (DC 13 Insight) becomes its first target.
A small chime rings when it is hurt, alerting every other celestial in the space.
A church will pay 5 spirit coins for each feather it sheds.
It sheds dim light, and shadows within 10 feet of it vanish.
It refuses to strike first and offers parley to anyone who lowers their weapon.
Its feathers or scales fall when it's hit and heal 1d4 hit points to whoever picks them up.
It can tell if a creature has broken an oath, and attacks oath-breakers first.
It sings, and the song gives its allies advantage on saves against fear.
It is lost and confused, sent from an astral space it doesn't understand.
Undead within 30 feet of it have disadvantage on attack rolls.

looks: A silver halo burns steadily above it, ringing faintly like a struck bell.
Its wings are overlapping silver blades that chime when they fold.
So luminous is it that lesser light sources seem dim beside it.
Its skin is pale as moonstone, with veins of silver light beneath.
Each of its eyes holds a tiny star that wheels slowly.
Ever-moving silver script is engraved across its armour, robes or hide.
A soft chorus trails it and swells when it fights.
Frost-white flowers bloom briefly in its footprints and fade within the hour.
Two pairs of wings sprout where its kind usually has one pair, or none.
Against darkness its outline glows silver like the rim of an eclipse.
quirks: It sees through illusions within 60 feet and points them out to everyone.
Once per encounter it speaks a word of command; one creature within 30 feet makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or drops what it holds.
It heals by singing; at the end of its turn, one ally within 30 feet regains 1d8 hit points.
It will not fight a creature that kneels before it, but it demands a vow in exchange.
Its strikes deal an extra {half} radiant damage to fiends and undead.
It feels every monster core in the room and goes straight for whoever carries the most.
When it dies, its body turns to silver light and leaves behind a single shining essence.
It carries a sealed message for someone in Greenstone and begs the party to deliver it.
Its radiance blinds: a creature that hits it in melee makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is blinded until the end of its next turn.
It judges the party by their deeds and fights harder against those with blood on their hands.
Once per encounter it heals an ally within 30 feet for {dmg} hit points.
It can't lie, and won't stop telling the party uncomfortable truths.
Its weapons deal radiant damage that ignores resistance.
Its wings beat up a wind that pushes creatures within 15 feet back 10 feet.
It carries a message for someone in the party and won't say who until the fight is over.

looks: Its halo has become a full ring of golden fire that circles its whole body.
Six wings of molten gold unfold from its back, each feather shedding sparks.
It towers and blazes, and looking at it for long makes the eyes water.
It seems carved from warm gold, its face a serene, unmoving mask.
Light pours from its mouth when it speaks, casting shadows behind its listeners.
Every surface it touches gleams as if freshly polished.
A ring of golden eyes opens across its wings when it is angered.
White-gold flame wreathes its weapons or claws without burning it.
Bells ring somewhere in the distance whenever it moves quickly.
The air around it is warm as a summer noon, even in a frozen space.
quirks: A creature that meets its gaze makes a DC {dc} Charisma save or can speak only the truth for 1 minute.
Creatures with sunlight sensitivity must pass a DC {dc} Constitution save each turn to come within 30 feet of it.
As a reaction, it can grant an ally within 30 feet a +2 bonus to AC against one attack.
If killed, it reforms at dawn in the space's heart unless its core is carried out of the space.
It speaks with the authority of a church; clergy in the party must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save to attack it first.
It knows the true layout of the space and will trade that knowledge for a promise.
Its wingbeats push creatures within 15 feet 10 feet away on a failed DC {dc} Strength save.
Fiends in the space fear it and avoid its rooms, making its territory strangely peaceful.
It is served by a choir of lesser lights that blind and distract.
Divine essences near it glow, and their bearers feel their god watching.
Any creature that dies within 30 feet of it rises at the end of the fight with 1 hit point, unless it chooses otherwise.
It speaks for a great astral being, and its words carry that being's weight.
Its blood is liquid light; a vial of it cures any disease.
Its presence makes lies hurt; a creature that lies within 60 feet takes {half} radiant damage.
It can't be harmed by a creature that has never killed.

looks: It is living light held in a shape, with a diamond core visible at its heart.
Countless wings of prismatic crystal fold around it like a temple window.
Behind it turns a great wheel of diamond that was once a halo.
Immense and silent, it sends shadows fleeing in every direction.
Rainbows spill from every edge of its body and paint the walls in shifting colour.
Its face changes to resemble someone each viewer trusts.
The ground beneath it turns to clear crystal that rings like a bell when walked on.
Stars are visible around it even indoors, as if it carries a sky with it.
Its voice is a choir of thousands and shakes dust from the ceiling.
No shadow falls anywhere within 30 feet of it.
quirks: Its presence hallows the room; undead and fiends that start their turn within 60 feet take {half} radiant damage.
Before battle it names each creature's greatest wrong aloud.
Once per encounter it can call on its god and return to full hit points, but only if it has harmed no innocent.
No creature within 30 feet of it can knowingly speak a falsehood.
Every church in the region feels its death, and priests will come asking questions.
It may offer a blessing instead of a fight: advantage on one saving throw each day for a week, in exchange for a quest.
Its wings blaze; creatures within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Constitution save at the start of their turn or are blinded until the end of it.
One of its feathers, set in a shrine, keeps undead away from a village for a year.
It is a fragment of a great astral being, and killing it angers the whole.
Its light reveals all things: invisible creatures, illusions and disguises fail within 120 feet.
Once per day it can restore a creature to life that died within the last minute.
It cannot be harmed by a creature it has forgiven, and forgives easily.
Its voice compels honesty; no creature within 60 feet can knowingly lie.
Its death causes dawn to break over the area, whatever the hour, for a full day.
It knows the name of everyone it meets, including their true one.

looks: Bronze plates are riveted over older iron across its whole body.
Blue sparks dance between the joints of its limbs when it moves.
A full head taller than standard models, it carries an extra plate of armour on its chest.
Its eyes are glowing amber crystals set in deep sockets.
A steady ticking comes from inside it, regular as a clock.
Verdigris has crept over its seams, turning it green at the edges.
One arm has been replaced with a heavier, mismatched limb.
Runes carved into its surface glow dull orange when it is active.
Steam vents from small holes in its back with each step.
It is painted in faded colours that once marked it as someone's guardian.
quirks: It follows an old command loop; a DC 13 Arcana check reveals the pattern and a pause the party can slip through.
Its gears grind loudly, so it can never surprise anyone.
It repairs itself slowly, regaining 2 hit points at the end of any turn in which it did not move.
A small hatch on its back holds a key or token tied to the space's heart.
Water makes it sluggish; while soaked, its speed drops by 10 feet.
It ignores anyone holding a particular symbol, which can be found elsewhere in the space.
When destroyed, it bursts into scrap that deals 1d6 piercing damage to creatures within 5 feet.
A smith in Greenstone will pay 10 spirit coins for its salvaged plating.
Its joints squeal loudly; it can't surprise anyone.
It follows old orders and will stop if told the right password.
Its core is set in a cage that can be pried out with a DC {dc} Strength check while it's grappled or prone.
It repairs itself slowly, regaining 5 hit points at the start of each turn unless it took lightning damage.
It ignores anyone not carrying a weapon.
Its plating hides a compartment holding its maker's notes.
Its maker's mark is on its chest, and the maker still lives.

looks: Its plates are polished silver steel that reflect the party in warped, stretched shapes.
A lattice of glowing silver wires shows through gaps in its armour.
Sleek and taller than any of its kind, it is built for speed as much as strength.
Its core shines through a crystal window in its chest, pulsing cold blue.
Runes flow across its surface like water, rearranging themselves as it fights.
Its limbs end in interchangeable tools that it swaps with a sharp click.
It moves with eerie smoothness, without the jerks and hitches of lesser constructs.
Fine silver dust drifts off it and coats the floor wherever it stands guard.
Its head is a smooth mask with a single sliding eye-slit.
A pure, high note hums from it and rises in pitch just before it strikes.
quirks: After it takes damage of a type, it has resistance to that type until the end of its next turn.
It links with other constructs within 60 feet and shares their senses.
It records everything it sees; a DC 15 Arcana check on its core replays the last hour.
It guards one room and will not pursue past its doorway.
Its eye beam marks a target, and the next attack against that creature by any construct has advantage.
The first time it takes lightning damage, it is stunned until the end of its next turn.
It politely asks for a password before attacking; the password is written somewhere in the space.
Its silver-steel frame is worth 50 spirit coins to the right buyer.
It learns: after it's hit by a damage type twice, it gains resistance to that type for the rest of the fight.
It can detach a limb to keep fighting on its own.
When reduced to 0 hit points it explodes, dealing {dmg} fire damage to all within 10 feet (DC {dc} Dexterity save for half).
Its eyes record everything it sees, and its maker can watch later.
It is immune to being knocked prone, pushed or pulled.
It guards one specific thing and will chase anyone who takes it to the ends of the earth.
It hums a tune its maker loved; anyone who knew them recognises it.

looks: Its gold-plated steel is engraved with scenes of forgotten wars.
It is enormous, and smaller constructs scurry around it oiling its joints.
A ring of golden gears turns slowly above its head like a crown.
Light pours from the seams of its armour, as if it is full of molten metal.
Its face is a perfect golden mask whose expression changes with its mood.
Arcs of lightning leap between the plates of its shoulders.
Its chest opens to reveal a spinning core of golden light.
Each footstep leaves a glowing rune that fades after a minute.
A tabard of a kingdom no one remembers is fused to its body by old heat.
Each of its four arms carries a different weapon.
quirks: Every hour, a new Iron-rank construct steps from its workshop.
It cannot be reasoned with, but it can be ordered; a creature that passes a DC 18 Arcana check may give it one command.
Bloodied, it overclocks: it gains an extra action each turn but takes {half} damage at the end of each of its turns.
A creature that studies it for an action and passes a DC 16 Investigation check finds a weak point, and its next hit is a critical hit.
It ignores the first effect each round that would move it against its will.
Its fists ring like great bells; a creature it hits makes a DC {dc} Constitution save or is deafened for 1 minute.
It knows the space's original maker and speaks of them only in reverent fragments.
It refuses to leave its post even while the space collapses around it.
It can reshape its body once per encounter, gaining a reach of 15 feet or a speed of 60 feet.
It shuts down any magic item within 10 feet of it, for as long as it stands.
It rebuilds itself from the parts of other constructs in its lair.
It has a second core; destroying the first only makes it angrier.
It speaks in its maker's voice, pleading to be left alone.
Its steps sink into stone; it can't be moved against its will.
Its body is made of a metal no smith has seen before.

looks: It is carved from a single flawless diamond, with machinery visible inside like a frozen storm.
It is the size of a tower, and its footsteps are felt in the next room.
Constellations of tiny gears orbit it like moons.
Its core is a captured star that makes every shadow in the room point away from it.
Its surface is so perfectly smooth that it reflects things that are not in the room.
Its joints are made of light rather than metal and bend in impossible directions.
Lines of glowing script scroll endlessly across its body, the record of its making.
It is utterly silent, without the slightest hum or tick.
A shell of crystal shards turns slowly around it.
Its eyes are prisms that cast the party's own colours back at them.
quirks: Unless its core is removed within a minute of its defeat, it rises again with half its hit points.
It runs the space; as a bonus action it can open, close or lock any door in the astral space.
It always knows which creature is most wounded, and targets them.
Each round it can copy one action a creature took last round, using its own statistics.
Spells of 3rd level or lower slide off its diamond surface without effect.
It holds the space's instructions; if it is destroyed, the space's special rules and traps stop working.
Its intact core could power a city's wards for a decade, and several factions will want it.
It has waited so long for a challenger that it salutes before every fight.
It is older than any kingdom and still follows the orders of a dead empire.
It can absorb a spell aimed at it once per round and recast it on its next turn.
Any construct within a mile obeys it.
It is building something, and it's almost finished.
It knows the true name of every essence and is trying to collect them.
Destroying it releases a flood of stored magic that changes the land around it.
It once served a great astral being and still waits for its master's return.

looks: Its scales are deep bronze with a green patina at the edges.
A row of extra horns juts from its brow like a crude crown.
Longer than others of its kind, it has a whiplike tail ending in a spur.
Smoke curls constantly from its nostrils, even when it is calm.
Its belly scales glow faintly, as if heated from within.
Its wings are ragged and scarred, but strong.
Its slit golden eyes follow coins more closely than faces.
A ridge of sharp plates runs down its spine.
Its claws are blackened as if dipped in soot.
Its scales have a hammered texture, like beaten metal.
quirks: It sleeps on a small hoard of 3d10 spirit coins and one trinket.
It demands tribute and will let a party pass for 20 spirit coins each.
It is vain; a creature that flatters it with a DC 13 Persuasion check delays its attack by one round.
Its breath leaves the ground smouldering for a minute, turning the area into difficult terrain.
It can smell spirit coins through solid stone.
Bloodied, it retreats to its hoard and fights to the death there.
It roars at dawn each day, a sound that echoes through the whole space.
Its shed scales make fine shield facings, worth 5 spirit coins each.
It hoards one thing (bells, books, swords) and will trade for more of it.
It is young and vain, and flattery buys a round's pause.
Its scales are loose; a hit of 18 or higher knocks one free, worth 2d10 spirit coins.
It breathes once, then fights in the air out of reach.
It speaks only to the strongest-looking member of the party.
It has a nest of eggs nearby and fights to the death to defend it.
Its blood is hot enough to burn: a creature that hits it in melee takes 1d4 fire damage.

looks: Its bright silver scales ring when struck, like coins in a purse.
Half again the size of its kind, it has a wingspan that fills a hall.
Pale light flickers in the back of its throat between breaths.
Its horns curve back in long silver spirals.
A thin line of glowing blue edges every scale.
Its eyes reflect the room like polished mirrors.
Its wings are translucent, showing a lattice of silver bones.
A cold mist pours off it, frosting the floor.
Its tail ends in a crescent-shaped blade of bone.
Lighter scales form a constellation along its back.
quirks: Its breath weapon recharges on a 4 or higher instead of the usual roll.
Clever and talkative, it knows rumours about other astral spaces and trades them for news.
When a creature moves behind it, it sweeps its tail as a reaction: DC {dc} Dexterity save or be knocked prone.
Its wingbeats snuff out torches and small flames within 30 feet.
It hoards magic items and can sense one within 120 feet.
When first bloodied, its scales flare, dealing {half} damage of its breath type to creatures within 10 feet.
It keeps a captive in its lair who knows the way to the heart.
It respects strength; if a creature lands a critical hit on it, it may stop and offer a deal.
It recharges its breath on a 4-6, not just a 5-6.
It claims the land around it as its own and demands tribute from travellers.
Its roar shakes loose rocks from cliffs; creatures below make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {dmg} bludgeoning damage.
It knows the names of local nobles and their secrets, and uses both.
Its scales reflect magic: the first spell attack against it each round has disadvantage.
It has bargained with a local noble house and is under their protection.
It is curious about outworlders and will stop fighting to ask one questions.

looks: Its scales are true gold, and its hide glitters like its own hoard.
It is vast, and its shadow alone covers a whole party.
A crown of golden horns rings its head, each etched with runes.
Fire runs like veins of lava beneath its gleaming scales.
Its eyes are molten pools that drip sparks when it is angry.
Lightning plays across its wings each time they unfold.
Weapons of slain adventurers still jut from its hide like trophies.
Its breath leaves glittering motes hanging in the air.
Its tail is long enough to coil twice around the room.
Gold edges its wings and hums in the wind.
quirks: Its presence terrifies; creatures within 60 feet make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or are frightened for 1 minute.
It has studied magic and knows two cantrips and one 3rd-level spell of the DM's choice.
On initiative count 20 the ceiling cracks and falls; creatures below make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {half} bludgeoning damage.
It never fights alone; lesser monsters of the space answer its call within two rounds.
It remembers everyone who has stolen from it and sends servants after them.
Anyone who takes from its hoard without killing it is hunted by its kin.
It offers a bargain: bring it the head of a rival from another astral space and keep a share of the hoard.
Its scales, worked into armour, are worth a small fortune to the Adventure Society's armourers.
Its wingbeats knock creatures within 15 feet prone (DC {dc} Strength save).
It hoards spirit coins and can sense them within a mile.
Its lair heats or chills to match its breath, and anyone without resistance gains a level of exhaustion each hour.
Lesser dragons serve it and bring it news.
It has outlived three adventuring teams that came for it, and keeps their gear on display.
Its scales are worth a fortune, and the Magic Society wants every one.
It never fights fairly; it knows the battlefield and uses every feature.

looks: Its scales are flawless diamond, and in any light it blazes so bright it must be fought half-blind.
It is so large that the astral space seems built around it.
Its breath glows through its translucent throat, a coiled storm of colour.
When its wings spread, they blot out the sky of the space and night falls.
Whole landscapes shift in its eyes each time it blinks.
Runes older than any known kingdom are carved into its horns.
Crystal grows wherever its blood falls, sharp and singing.
Its every breath stirs a wind that carries the scent of distant places.
A slowly turning ring of floating treasure surrounds it.
Its scales show reflections of past battles, moving like memories.
quirks: The space's weather follows its mood, turning to storm or calm as it pleases.
It speaks every language and knows each adventurer's name before they enter.
Its breath scars the air; the area deals {half} damage of that type to anything that ends its turn there for the next hour.
It can take three lair actions each round instead of one.
It has watched the party through the space and knows their favourite tactics before the fight begins.
Its hoard and body are worth more than most cities, and word of its death spreads within a week.
It may spare a party that amuses it, demanding a story for each life.
The first time each creature damages it, that creature makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or is frightened of it for the rest of the encounter.
It is old enough to remember the world before the current churches.
Its breath changes the land permanently: grass never grows where it burned.
It has a legendary action pool one larger than its stat block shows.
It speaks with the authority of a ruler, and some cities still pay it tribute.
Its hoard includes an awakening stone of every affinity.
It knows how to unmake essences, and threatens to.
Killing it is the work of a generation, and the Society keeps a file on it.

looks: Its body churns with darker, denser matter than usual, like a cloud heavy with rain.
A dull bronze core glows through its elemental body.
It is a head taller than others of its kind and more solid at the edges.
Debris orbits it slowly: pebbles, sparks, droplets or torn leaves.
Its colour is wrong for its element: greenish flame, red water, black wind.
A faint humming rises from it, like a kettle about to boil.
Its edges flicker between two elements, never quite settling.
It leaves a trail of scorched, soaked or scoured ground.
Two small points of white light serve as its eyes.
Its surface ripples constantly, as if something swims inside it.
quirks: It is drawn to its own element and ignores the party if a bigger fire, pool or draught is nearby to feed on.
Within a minute of its arrival, the room's temperature shifts by 20 degrees.
Its touch ignites or snuffs out small unattended objects, depending on its element.
When killed, it leaves an ember, puddle or pile of grit that alchemists will buy for 10 spirit coins.
Reduced to 0 hit points, it splits into two Iron-rank elementals of the same kind.
Once per encounter it sinks into its element and rises 30 feet away.
Its roar drowns out speech; casting a spell with a verbal component within 10 feet of it takes a DC 12 Constitution save.
It is bound to its room, and calms a minute after the party leaves it.
Its element seeps into the ground: the area within 10 feet of it becomes difficult terrain after it stays there a round.
It is bound to a place and can't move more than 300 feet from it.
It flickers between solid and not; nonmagical weapons deal half damage to it.
It is drawn to its own element and grows stronger near it.
It speaks only in its element's language, and a druid can calm it.
It was summoned and abandoned; whoever summoned it is nearby.
Its core holds a little of its element and can be used as a bomb once.

looks: Silver light pulses at its heart, and its element swirls around it like a slow whirlpool of stars.
It towers over its kind, its body shaped into crude limbs and a featureless face.
Its element has crystallised in places into silver-white shards.
Arcs of energy leap from its body to nearby metal.
Between motions it is perfectly still, without a flicker.
Its colour is a cold, clear silver tinted with its element's hue.
Small storms of its element form and burst around it.
Its core is visible as a spinning silver stone.
The ground under it becomes its element in a 10-foot circle.
It hums with a tone that rattles teeth and makes armour buzz.
quirks: Damage of its own element heals it for half the amount instead of harming it.
Each round it reshapes the battlefield, turning a 10-foot square into difficult terrain.
Once per encounter it bursts; creatures within 15 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or take {half} damage of its element.
When first bloodied, it calls up a lesser elemental of its kind.
It moves through any amount of its element as if through open air.
Its core holds a spark of pure element that the Magic Society pays well for.
It hates its opposing element and attacks whoever carries it first.
It speaks in the sound of its element and can be bargained with by anyone who knows Primordial.
It splits in two when bloodied, each half with half its remaining hit points.
It absorbs damage of its own element, healing instead.
Its aura of element deals {half} damage to any creature that starts its turn within 5 feet.
It moves through its element as if it were air.
It can turn into a cloud or puddle of its element, becoming hard to see and hit.
It changes the weather in a mile around it while it lives.
It is angry about a wrong done to its place, and a fix will end the fight.

looks: Its golden core blazes like a small sun, and its element surges around it in great waves.
It is huge, and the room strains to contain it.
It has taken a regal shape, with a crown of its element above its head.
Gold veins of energy run through its form and pulse when it moves.
The air around it shimmers and warps as if under great pressure.
Its element burns almost white, with gold at the edges.
Small elementals orbit it like attendants.
Each step it takes turns the ground to its element.
Its voice is rumbling stone, roaring flame or crashing surf.
Its outline is perfectly sharp, as if cut out of the world.
quirks: Its weather follows it; rain, gales, heat or tremors fill any room it enters.
A creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of it takes {half} damage of its element.
As a bonus action it can swap places with any lesser elemental in the space.
On initiative count 20 a wall, pit or wave of its element appears where it chooses.
Spells of its element cast within 60 feet are drawn into it, granting it temporary hit points equal to the damage.
It is ancient and speaks of the time before the space was made.
When it dies, its element erupts in a 30-foot radius; DC {dc} Dexterity save, {dmg} damage, half on a success.
An old pact binds it; reciting its true name, carved somewhere in the space, ends the fight.
It summons 1d4 lesser elementals of its kind once per encounter.
Its element bursts out when it's hit hard: any hit of 20 or more creates a 10-foot-radius burst of {dmg} damage.
It is the heart of a natural wonder and the wonder fades if it dies.
It can't be harmed while touching its element.
Its voice is a storm, an earthquake or a wildfire, and it speaks often.
It holds a grudge against the Magic Society for binding its kin.
It will bargain for its freedom from a bond.

looks: Its core is a perfect diamond holding a storm, a sea, a fire or a mountain inside it.
It is as large as the room it fills, and the room seems shaped around it.
Its element flows in impossible ways: fire that drips, water that burns, stone that floats.
Rainbow light refracts through its crystal heart and paints the space.
A ring of eerie calm surrounds it where nothing moves.
Lightning, flame, water and stone all flicker briefly through its body.
Its body is so dense that light bends around it.
Its presence is felt across the whole space as a pressure in the ears.
Its face is a slowly turning vortex that seems to look at everyone at once.
Wherever it moves, its element lingers for days.
quirks: The astral space is its body; it can attack from any room filled with its element.
It cannot be grappled, restrained or moved against its will.
Its roar sets off disasters across the space: floods, fires, quakes or storms.
Once per encounter it forms a Silver-rank elemental servant from its own body.
At half hit points it shifts to a second element and gains that element's resistances.
Its core can power a relic or anchor a city ward, and is treasure beyond price.
Creatures within 120 feet of it have disadvantage on saving throws against its element.
It has no malice, only hunger, and can be lured away by a great offering of its element.
It is an elemental lord's lieutenant, and its master is watching.
It turns the land around it into its element for a mile.
It regenerates fully unless its element is cut off from it.
Killing it releases its element in a disaster: a flood, quake, firestorm or gale.
It can reshape the terrain each round as a bonus action.
It remembers the world's making and has opinions about it.
It can grant a person a trace of its element as a blessing, if pleased.

looks: Its skin or fur has a faint bronze shimmer, like autumn leaves in low sun.
Tiny flowers grow in its hair and close when it is angry.
Its eyes are a bright, unnatural green, with flecks that drift.
A little taller and thinner than its kind, it has long, restless fingers.
Glittering dust falls from it when it moves.
Its shadow is the shape of a different creature.
A scent of crushed mint and rain follows it.
Little bells seem to ring when it laughs, though it carries none.
Thorny vines twist around its limbs like jewellery.
Its long ears twitch toward any sound of music.
quirks: It loves riddles and trades safe passage for a good one (DC 13 Intelligence check to compose one it likes).
It steals small things; each creature that comes within 5 feet of it loses a trinket.
It cannot abide cold iron and flees from anyone brandishing a cold-iron weapon.
It laughs when hurt, and the laughter heals allies within 30 feet for 1d4 hit points.
As a bonus action, it can teleport 10 feet, always to a spot behind someone.
It speaks only in rhyme and takes offence when answered plainly.
Its food is delicious and harmless, but whoever eats it must tell the truth for an hour.
It pays 1d10 spirit coins to anyone who dances with it, though the coins may be leaves by dawn.
It plays tricks rather than kills: stealing boots, swapping weapons, tying laces together.
It must answer any question asked three times in a row.
It can't cross running water or a line of salt.
It's bound to honour a bargain if one is offered and accepted.
Iron weapons deal an extra 1d4 damage to it.
It knows the party's names and uses them to mock.
It leaves a gift if it is treated with courtesy.

looks: Its skin shines with a moonlit silver sheen, and its eyes reflect stars.
Delicate wings of silver light flicker on its back.
Flowers bloom ahead of its feet and wilt behind it in a perfect trail.
Its outline is slightly blurred, as if seen in a dream.
Its hair or mane drifts as if underwater.
Silver antlers hung with dewdrops grow from its brow.
Its colouring cycles through the seasons over a single fight.
Larger than its kind, it moves with a dancer's grace.
Moths and fireflies circle it in slow orbits.
Its clothing or fur looks woven from spider silk and moonlight.
quirks: Once per encounter it beguiles a creature: DC {dc} Wisdom save or the target sees it as a trusted friend for 1 minute.
Any bargain made with it is magically binding on both sides.
Its glamour hides the room's true exits; a DC 15 Investigation check reveals them.
It steps into any tree, flower or mushroom and out of another within 60 feet.
Each time it is hit, an illusory double of it appears, up to three at once; an attack on a double ends it.
It hungers for mortal names and tries to learn each creature's full name.
It hosts a revel each night; guests are safe from harm but lose a day of time outside.
When killed, it leaves a seed that grows into a small, gentle copy of itself within a year.
Once per encounter it charms a creature for a minute (DC {dc} Wisdom negates); the charmed creature thinks it is a lost friend.
It can turn invisible until it attacks.
It steals a memory with each hit, and gives them back if paid.
Its dance forces those who watch to join in (DC {dc} Wisdom save).
Time runs differently near it; each minute in its circle is an hour outside.
It can swap shapes with a nearby animal.
It owes a debt to someone in the party's past.

looks: A crown of golden leaves that never fall rests on its head, and its skin glows like late afternoon.
Its beauty is painful to look at, and its face is hard to recall afterward.
It is tall and regal, with a cloak of living flowers trailing behind it.
Golden pollen hangs in the air around it and glitters in torchlight.
Its eyes change colour to match whatever the viewer loves most.
Its shadow is a whole crowd of dancing figures.
Grass pushes through the stone around it until the room becomes a glade.
A court of small fey follows it, mimicking its every gesture.
Seasons turn around it: blossom, then fruit, then falling leaves.
Soft music plays wherever it walks, though no musicians are seen.
quirks: Once per round, one creature that can hear it makes a DC {dc} Charisma save or obeys a one-word command.
Time runs strangely near it; each hour spent in its presence is a day outside.
It cannot break a promise, and it uses this to trap others into making them.
It can swap places with any plant in the space at will.
The first time it is hurt, every plant in the room turns hostile for 1 minute.
It proposes a game; a party that wins may claim one modest favour.
Creatures it has charmed remember it fondly forever and may seek it out years later.
Its tears are a prized alchemical ingredient; each one sells for 100 spirit coins.
It rules a small court of lesser fey, all of whom will defend it.
It can only be harmed by a creature who has spoken its true name.
It traps creatures in illusions; the first time each creature is hit, DC {dc} Intelligence save or believes it is somewhere else for a round.
It grants wishes, badly.
Its kiss puts a creature to sleep for a hundred years, unless woken.
It can curse a whole bloodline.
Its wings scatter dust that makes creatures float 10 feet into the air.

looks: It is made of light and memory, and each viewer sees it slightly differently.
A diamond crown floats above it, scattering rainbows that turn into butterflies.
Immense and graceful, it makes every movement look like part of a dance.
Whole seasons cycle across its body in moments.
Its eyes show each viewer their own future, or a lie about it.
Gardens of flowers no one has ever seen grow from its back.
It casts no shadow, but the shadows of everyone around it bow.
Its voice is a song some of the party remember from childhood.
The space around it fades into a dreamscape at the edges.
Its skin is clear as crystal, with starlight running through it like veins.
quirks: Its presence blurs what is real; each round, creatures within 60 feet make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or treat one random ally as an illusion until their next turn.
Ancient rules of hospitality bind it; it cannot attack a guest who has accepted its food.
It can rewrite one memory of each creature that hears its voice.
It may offer a true gift, such as a second shadow, a stolen year or a singing voice, each with a hidden cost.
If it is killed, every fey in the region mourns, and the land remembers the killers.
It knows the history of every astral space it has passed through and tells it as a story.
It plays games with lives, but always gives a fair chance to win.
As an action it vanishes from every mind in the room for 1 minute; a DC {dc} Intelligence save notices it.
It is a ruler of a fey realm, and harming it is an act of war.
It can steal a person's face, name or voice permanently.
It can turn a season inside out across a whole region.
Its bargains bind gods.
It can bring the party into its realm with a word, and out again only on its terms.
It has been watching the party for a long time and has plans for them.
It cannot die, only be banished for a century.

looks: Its skin is dark bronze, cracked like cooling metal, with red light in the cracks.
An extra pair of horns curls forward from its head like hooks.
It reeks of brimstone so strongly that eyes water at 10 feet.
Its eyes are coals that flare when it smiles.
Bigger than its kind, it has a barrel chest and long arms.
Its tail ends in a barbed hook that drips something black.
Wisps of smoke curl from its skin whenever it is hurt.
Its teeth are needle-thin and far too numerous.
Strange brands mark its skin, glowing faintly in patterns.
Its shadow flickers like firelight even in darkness.
quirks: It offers deals constantly, each slightly worse than the last.
It can smell a lie and goes first for anyone who has lied in the last day.
Holy water deals it an extra 1d6 damage and makes it flee for one round.
It taunts in a creature's own voice and has advantage on its next Deception check.
When it dies, it leaves a scorch mark shaped like a grin that lasts for weeks.
Once per encounter it calls a swarm of biting flies that fills a 10-foot cube and lightly obscures it.
It keeps a list of names it has collected and is eager to add more.
Its blood corrodes metal; a weapon that hits it takes a -1 penalty until repaired.
It offers a deal before it fights, and the deal is almost fair.
It smells of sulphur and leaves scorched hoofprints.
Holy water burns it for 2d6 radiant damage.
It feeds on anger; it gains advantage against creatures that hit it in a rage.
It knows one secret about each party member.
It was summoned by a cultist who's still nearby.
It can't enter a home without being invited.

looks: Its skin is black and polished like obsidian, with silver runes carved across it.
Chains of silver light wrap its arms and rattle when it moves.
Tall and elegant, it wears a cruel, handsome face.
Its leathery wings are edged with silver flame.
Its eyes are white-hot silver points that leave afterimages.
Its horns have grown into a jagged silver crown.
Shadows pool at its feet and stain the floor where it stands.
Its voice is soft and pleasant, but the words leave a bitter taste in listeners' mouths.
A ring of scorched glyphs forms on the ground wherever it rests.
The marks of old bindings are burned into its skin.
quirks: A creature that talks with it makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or agrees to one small, odd request.
It knows each creature's deepest want and offers it in exchange for a favour.
It can step into any fire and out of another within 120 feet.
Wounds it deals do not heal naturally until treated with a DC 13 Medicine check or magic.
Radiant damage makes it shriek, and every fiend in the space learns where it is.
It keeps stolen souls in a small silver box that a church will pay well to destroy.
A contract hidden in the space binds it here, and tearing the contract banishes it.
Once per encounter, when hit, it swaps places with an ally within 30 feet, who takes the hit instead.
Its wounds spray burning blood; any creature that hits it in melee takes {half} fire damage.
It possesses a fallen foe's body when reduced to 0 hit points (DC {dc} Charisma save to resist for a creature still alive).
It speaks in the voice of a lost loved one.
It can't be harmed by a creature it has made a bargain with.
It summons a lesser fiend when bloodied.
Its presence spoils food and turns milk.
It's bound by a contract and is looking for a loophole.

looks: Its skin is gilded and gleaming, like a statue of a beloved hero gone rotten.
Great wings of golden fire spread from its back.
Huge and regal, it wears a crown of burning golden horns.
Golden chains hang from it, each ending in a screaming face.
Its eyes are molten gold, and gold tears run down its cheeks.
The ground cracks and glows beneath its hooves.
Lesser fiends kneel in a ring around it.
Gilded contracts are carved into its body, every line a deal it won.
Smoke rises from it in the shapes of faces.
Its voice is beautiful and warm, and listeners long to agree.
quirks: Creatures that start their turn within 30 feet make a DC {dc} Wisdom save or are frightened until the end of that turn.
Once per day it can seal a binding contract with anyone who agrees, even under duress.
Once per encounter it summons a Bronze-rank fiend.
Each creature it kills heals it for {half} hit points.
It knows the name of every adventurer who has entered the space and calls them out.
Its blood burns; creatures that hit it with a melee attack take 1d6 fire damage.
The churches post a bounty for proof of its death.
At half hit points it offers to surrender in exchange for its life, and the offer is sincere.
It corrupts divine essences: a creature with one that it hits makes a DC {dc} Wisdom save or loses access to its divine powers for a day.
It returns to life a tenday after death unless its name is struck from its contract.
Its lair is a pocket of another place where fire falls as rain.
It can see through the eyes of anyone who has made a deal with it.
It has a cult in the nearest city.
It can only be truly killed with a blessed weapon.
It whispers to the weakest party member each night.

looks: Its body is cut from black diamond, and countless trapped fires burn in its depths.
It is vast, and its presence makes the walls sweat and the air thicken.
A ring of diamond horns crowns it, casting red light.
Its wings are made of burning contracts that flutter like pages.
Each of its eyes holds a tiny prisoner pleading for release.
Its footprints are pools of molten stone.
Its face shifts to resemble a hated enemy of each viewer.
It casts many shadows, each shaped like a soul it owns.
Rain stops above it and hisses into steam before it falls.
Its voice is a whisper heard directly in the mind.
quirks: It sees the price of every soul and names what each adventurer is worth.
A creature that drops to 0 hit points within 60 feet of it makes a DC {dc} Charisma save or rises as its servant for 1 minute.
It can turn any fire in the space into a doorway it alone may use.
Its deals are upheld by powers greater than itself, and breaking one brings ruinous luck.
When it dies, its trapped souls are freed and may help or haunt the party.
It holds a key to another astral space inside its heart.
It treats the fight as a game and gives the party a one-round head start.
Holy weapons deal an extra {half} radiant damage to it, but each hit cracks the weapon a little.
It is a power in its own right, served by cults across the world.
Its true name could bind it, if anyone could find it.
It owns the soul of someone important.
Killing it frees a thousand bound spirits at once, and some are dangerous.
It can corrupt a whole town's water, food or wine.
It walks unseen among mortals as a respected figure.
It's been bargaining with an astral power, and the bargain is nearly complete.

looks: Its skin has the grain and colour of weathered bronze.
A full head taller than its kin, it drags its knuckles.
Moss and lichen grow in the cracks of its skin.
One eye is milky and blind; the other is bright and wary.
A crude bronze collar is fused to its neck.
Its beard is braided with bones and spirit coins.
It carries a tree trunk as a club, roots still attached.
Its skin is rough as rock and covered in old scratches.
Thick tusks jut from its lower jaw.
It wears armour made from a cart and several doors.
quirks: It throws rocks at anything that moves on the horizon, giving away its position.
Lonely, it will talk before fighting if offered food.
It counts poorly and can be fooled into thinking the party is twice its size.
Each time it stamps, creatures within 10 feet make a DC {dc} Dexterity save or fall prone.
It keeps a pet, a lesser beast, and defends it fiercely.
Its lair holds a pile of dented helmets from lost adventurers, one of them still enchanted.
It sleeps deeply; a party can sneak past with a DC 12 Stealth check.
It hates being called small, and taunting it makes it charge blindly.
It throws whatever is to hand: rocks, trees, cows.
It is slow-witted and can be tricked with a riddle.
It's after food, and a big enough meal will send it away.
Its club is an old ship's mast.
It's young and away from home for the first time.
Its footfalls give it away a mile off.
It collects shiny buttons and trades favours for them.

looks: Its skin is pale silver-grey, like a mountain at dusk.
Frost forms on its skin and beard, and its breath fogs.
Half again the size of its kin, it is broad as a house.
Silver runes are tattooed across its arms and glow when it fights.
Its long hair is wind-whipped, even indoors.
It wears the shells of great beasts as armour.
Its pale blue eyes glint like ice.
